newsitem.title: USA: Breakdown of New York State joblessness by market.
newsitem.headline: Breakdown of New York State joblessness by market.

text.p: The following list details the February unemployment rates in various labor markets in New York State, according to a report released on Tuesday by the state Department of Labor.
--Albany-Schenectady-Troy, 4.7 pct in Feb, down from 4.8 in Jan and 5.6 a year ago.
--Binghamton, 5.0 pct, flat with Jan, and down from 5.6 pct a year ago.
--Buffalo-Niagara Falls, 5.8 pct, flat with Jan and down from 6.0 a year ago.
--Dutchess County, 4.6 pct, flat with Jan and down from 5.0 pct a year ago.
--Elmira, 4.4 pct, down from 4.6 pct in Jan and 5.0 pct a year-ago.
--Glens Falls, 8.2 pct, up from 8.0 pct in Jan, but down from 8.5 pct a year ago.
--Nassau-Suffolk, 4.0 pct, flat with Jan, but down from 4.9 pct a year-ago.
--Newburgh, NY, Orange County, 4.5 pct, up from 4.4 pct in Jan but down from 5.0 pct in Feb.
--New York City
Bronx, 12.1 pct, up from 12.0 pct in Jan and 10.3 pct a year-ago.
Kings, 11.3 pct, down from 11.4 pct in Jan and from 10.2 pct a year ago.
New York (Manhattan) 7.9 pct, down from 8.2 pct in Jan but up from 7.3 pct a year ago.
Queens, 9.2 pct, up from 9.0 pct in Jan and 8.6 pct a year-ago.
Richmond (Staten Island), 8.6 pct, up from 8.4 pct in Jan and 7.7 pct a year ago.
--New York Area
Putnam, 3.4 pct, flat with Jan and down from 4.1 pct a year ago.
Rockland, 4.0 pct, down from 4.1 pct in Jan and 4.6 pct a year ago.
Westchester, 4.1 pct, flat with Jan but down from 4.6 pct a year ago.
--Rochester, 4.4 pct, flat with Jan but down from 4.7 pct a year ago.
--Syracuse, 5.4 pct, down from 5.5 pct in Jan and 6.1 pct a year ago.
--Utica-Rome, 5.9 pct, down from 6.1 pct in Jan and 6.6 pct in Feb.
